next_question: Can a real HTTP measurement protocol (Flask server with PyJWT HS256 and real session cookies, behavioral signals derived from actual jwt.decode failures and HTTP 401/403 responses) demonstrate that session-level behavioral signals detect auth-state drift with TP>=0.9 while tolerating structural noise with FP<=0.15, and does the C4 orthogonality criterion survive when both signals are measured on the same stochastic conditions without block-zero imputation?
why_next: The behavioral signal experiment is MEASUREMENT_INVALID: signals were computed analytically by pattern name (not measured from HTTP), C4 Pearson r was computed on block-zero imputed vectors (guaranteed negative by construction), and AUC=1.0 is tautological. No empirical evidence about behavioral signals was accumulated. The parent handoff identified behavioral signals as the highest-upside untested alternative; this experiment failed to test them due to measurement methodology, not because the hypothesis was evaluated. A corrected experiment with real HTTP substrate is the minimum next step to either validate or falsify the behavioral dimension. If behavioral signals also fail on real HTTP, the C-FRESHNESS domain will have exhausted all single-signal-family approaches in deterministic mock and must pivot to fundamentally different designs (real API deployments with stochasticity, production traffic, or composite multi-signal classifiers on live data).

established: Six structural/schema-based signal families tested and all falsified for C-FRESHNESS frozen gate in deterministic mock: Jaccard (EXP-GRAPH-34788722106), TF-IDF (EXP-GRAPH-35010853847), response-time KS (EXP-GRAPH-35083040517), linear Fisher LDA ensemble (EXP-GRAPH-35130682058), field-usage profiling (EXP-GRAPH-35137034388), direct schema comparison (EXP-GRAPH-35154724244).
Schema diff is orthogonal to Jaccard structural similarity: Pearson r=-0.590 across 40 conditions. Schema diff captures required_to_optional drift (diff=0.3, Jaccard=1.0) which Jaccard cannot detect.

The magnitude confound is structural: optional_field_addition noise at 10% of schema size scales diff magnitude linearly with schema size (1.0-5.0), dominating subtle drift (required_to_optional 0.3) at all sizes.
C4 type-aware validation failure is measurement-invalid (mock conformance tautology), not evidence against type-aware detection.
Field-usage profiling provides orthogonal discrimination for field-availability drift with Pearson r=-0.045 to Jaccard, but fails on change_type (usage_similarity=1.0).
Noise immunity for unused fields across all experiments is a construction artefact — noise generators add fields no client requests.
rejected: Direct schema comparison as standalone drift-vs-noise discriminator (C2 fails under frozen rule)
Any single structural/schema-based signal family providing complete C-FRESHNESS discrimination — six families tested, all fail frozen gate
Unbounded optional field addition noise (10% of schema size) tolerable by schema diff or Jaccard — both fail at all schema sizes
Linear Fisher LDA ensemble of structural signals rescuing individual failures — AUC=0.625, all conditions fail
unknown: Whether session-level behavioral signals measured via real HTTP (not analytical assignment) detect auth drift with TP>=0.9 and tolerate structural noise with FP<=0.15
Whether behavioral signals measured on stochastic conditions (not block-zero imputation) achieve Pearson r<0.3 with structural signals (orthogonality)
Whether bounded optional field addition (max 1-2 fields) allows structural signals to pass C2
Whether composite multi-signal classifiers (schema diff + usage profiling + session signals) achieve discrimination none achieve individually
Whether real APIs with stochastic field availability, DB/cache/CDN variation, and heterogeneous client profiles preserve any discrimination gaps measured in deterministic mock
Whether the magnitude confound is intrinsic to deterministic mock settings or also affects real API deployments
do_not_assume: C-FRESHNESS is globally closed or rejected — six bounded signal families falsified in specific deterministic mock settings; the broader domain remains open
Behavioral signals are falsified for C-FRESHNESS — this experiment is MEASUREMENT_INVALID; the hypothesis is untested, not rejected
Session-level behavioral signals will succeed — they are orthogonal by dimension but their actual discrimination is untested on real HTTP; they may have their own confounds
Deterministic mock server results transfer to real APIs — all seven tested signals used the same deterministic mock; real APIs may shift discrimination gaps in either direction
The analytical behavioral result (TP=1.0 FP=0.0) is meaningful — it is tautological by construction and provides no empirical evidence
Bounded noise (max 1-2 optional fields) would pass C2 — plausible but untested
Per-sample features would show different results than aggregated means — all experiments used zero within-condition variance

recommended_action: Design a graph lane experiment that measures session-level behavioral signals via real HTTP: start a Flask server with PyJWT HS256 signing and real session cookies, issue real tokens via jwt.encode, validate via jwt.decode against current signing key, derive behavioral signals from actual HTTP 401/403 responses and Set-Cookie inspection (not analytical branching). Fix C4 orthogonality by computing Pearson r on conditions where both behavioral and structural signals are non-trivially measured (co-occurring drift+noise conditions, or per-sample variation within conditions). Add per-sample variation (token expiry timing jitter, session TTL variation, permission probe ordering) to enable Wilson CIs and per-sample ROC. Add co-occurring drift+noise conditions (auth change + field additions simultaneously). If behavioral signals also fail on real HTTP, the C-FRESHNESS domain has exhausted single-signal-family approaches in deterministic mock and must pivot to real API deployments with DB/cache/CDN stochasticity, production client traffic patterns, or composite multi-signal classifiers on live data.
